newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Strike hit Mondi mill has no supply problem.
newsitem.headline: Strike hit Mondi mill has no supply problem.

text.p: South African paper firm Mondi, a unit of Anglo American Industrial Corp Ltd, said on Thursday that a strike at its Merebank Mill would not cause supply problems to its customers.
The strike at the plant is part of an action by the Paper, Printing, Wood and Allied Workers' Union (PPWAWU) over wages.
It began on Wednesday night after wage talks broke down.

"(The mill) has strong stockholdings and does not anticipate major difficulties in continuing to supply customers. We have plans in place to maintain our production capacity at as high a level as possible for the duration of the strike," the firm said in a statement.
The Merebank mill is near Durban in the Indian Ocean province of KwaZulu-Natal.
Mondi Paper general manager said management was willing to return to the negotiating table.
"We remain willing to continue negotiations with PPWAWU representatives at any time," he said.
